component.name: BelfrySCAD
component.summary: Script-based 3D CAD you can also drag

description.p: BelfrySCAD is a procedural CAD application that runs the OpenSCAD language and keeps the code and the 3D model in step. Edit the script and the model follows; drag a shape in the viewport and the script rewrites itself.

ul.li: The full OpenSCAD language, with OpenSCAD-compatible .scad files
Click a shape to select the call you wrote, then move, rotate or scale it with a gizmo
Step any number or expression with the arrow keys and watch the model change
A debugger with breakpoints, a call stack and variable inspection
A Customizer for a script's parameters, with saved parameter sets
Library management, documentation generation, and a test runner with coverage
Export to 3MF, STL, OBJ, AMF, OFF, PLY, VRML, X3D and POV-Ray, and SVG, PDF and DXF for 2D designs

Selecting a shape highlights the call that made it

description.p: Move a single turtle path point without disturbing the rest, crash backups of unsaved edits, an argument hint that stays up while typing, and exports that remember their folder and format.
Split and straighten sections of a turtle path without moving the rest, and gizmo drags made while the last one is still rendering are no longer lost.
A 3D turtle editor for BOSL2's turtle3d(), and reference images on any plane and reference models to trace over in the 3D path, turtle and VNF editors.

Optional auto-closing brackets and indenting with tabs, shortcuts edited in place in Preferences, Tab rebindable, rotate and scale drags that commit about the part's centre without jumping, and turtle editor and stereo fixes.
Ctrl+/ toggles line comments the way VS Code does, Comment and Uncomment add or remove exactly one //, and Preferences has VS Code's two comment options.
A polyhedron whose duplicate vertices fall on a rounding boundary is no longer reported as open, and projection(cut=true) fills a slice where a shape overlaps itself, as OpenSCAD does.
Preferences has a Keyboard pane for changing any command's shortcut; the standard shortcuts such as Cut, Copy, Paste and Save stay fixed.

Quick Export on F7 reuses the last export's format and options (Animate moves to F9). The turtle editor gets a movable start, read from and written to turtle()'s state=, and joints that can be dragged while the arcs stay tangent; it saves one command per line. The path editor's NURBS Interpolated mode gets corners, read from and written to nurbs_interp(). Undocked panes on Windows and Linux get minimize and maximize, and Window > Dock All Panes re-docks them.
A module that picks its children by index, such as BOSL2's attachable(), now sees variables assigned in the child block. Edit as and View as work on a list that contains comments.
A variable reassigned after an include now reaches every value the library derives from it, as in OpenSCAD, and no longer warns. Cmd-click or right-click an include or use statement to open the file.

A turtle path editor for BOSL2 turtle() command lists: a command table beside a live preview, and click-to-draw lines, tangent arcs and jumps. Path lines in the editors are wider, and the default theme's axes are dark gray.
The x86_64 Flatpak starts again, opening a file from the desktop reaches the running window over D-Bus on Linux, and a path editor's background image now lies under the shape.
3MF files written by OpenSCAD and most slicers now import, and gizmo drags on Windows edit the right place in the code.
Create paths, regions and other shapes from the editor's right-click menu, build them point by point, drag vertices without Cmd, and right-drag panning works again in the editors.
The orientation cube now appears in every 3D data viewer and editor, not only the main window.
A background image to trace over in the 2D path and region editors, placed, scaled and rotated from the editor's right-click menu or by dragging its handles.
The diagnostic report for a window that stops responding now says whether the window is still being drawn and which input last reached it.
Translucent % and # parts no longer flicker where they lie on a solid face, and turning axis scales off hides the tick marks as well as the numbers.
The Color List is now a dock panel where you edit your palettes in place and insert a color into the script, and Choose Color… opens it on the color under the cursor.
Your own color palettes, such as the filament on your shelf, in the color picker and the Color List, which now also offers Web and XKCD colors separately.
Design ▸ Reload and Render (F4) picks up a file changed on disk and renders it, and Automatic Reload notices changes to used and included libraries more reliably, including on Windows.
A closing brace, bracket or parenthesis typed on a blank line now lines up with the line that opened it.
With word wrap on, a wrapped line's first character lines up with every other line's instead of sitting a few pixels to the left.
An if statement that takes its branch counts as an operand of intersection() even when it draws nothing, as in OpenSCAD, so BOSL2's partition() can show one piece alone.
levelset() meshes every 3D field on a regular grid, as BOSL2's isosurface() does, so function fields and per-axis edges no longer look dimpled.
Automatic Reload and Render also watches the files a model uses or includes, and is now first in the Design menu.
An error in the console is highlighted on its own line, no longer buried in a highlighted backtrace; interface text uses American spellings.
Font favorites are now individual faces: hearting a family's Regular no longer hearts every style of it.
Favorite and recently used fonts in the Font List and the font picker, and levelset() can place a field array from its sample spacing alone.
levelset() accepts infinite samples in a field and produces much smoother surfaces, and release-notes links to version comparisons now open the whole comparison.
A clearer Render toolbar icon (a page of code becoming a solid), and the view buttons' tooltips now read "View from Top" and so on.
Help ▸ Show Release Notes… and a Release Notes… button in the About box show the notes for every release up to the one installed.
The About box and --info report the installed Qt bindings (PySide6-Essentials) instead of saying PySide6 is not installed.
With line wrapping on, the end of a file can be scrolled to again past a very long line, and levelset() takes edge as one spacing per axis.
The toolbar and panel toggles (Show Editor, Show Console and the rest) moved from the top of the View menu to the end of the Window menu.
A render that produces no geometry now clears the viewport instead of leaving the previous shape on screen.
File Open now starts in the folder of the last file opened by any means, including Recent Files, a double-click and a drop.
OFF, OBJ, 3MF, X3D and VRML files whose triangles do not share vertices now import as closed solids, and X3D/VRML Switch and LOD import only their active child.
AMF files whose triangles do not share vertices now import as closed solids, as in OpenSCAD.
The default roof() now roofs unions of touching pieces, where it gave nothing or ran out of memory.

SVG and DXF import match OpenSCAD and a failed import no longer stops the render; roof(method="straight") builds a true straight-skeleton roof; messages are worded as OpenSCAD words them; BOSL2 evaluates as fast as before 1.68; new viewport colour schemes; code derived from OpenSCAD GPL source is replaced by clean-room reimplementations.
Builtin functions, assert(), let(), ranges, children() and textmetrics() now give the same values as OpenSCAD, finishing the builtin parity fixes.

Builtins now behave as OpenSCAD's do in dozens of cases that were silently different -- rotate_extrude, offset, surface, transforms of 2D shapes, modifiers in booleans and more -- two crashes are fixed, and models mixing 2D and 3D export as OpenSCAD renders them.

Subtracting a shape from an identical copy of itself, or an octa-style sphere from a rotated copy, now leaves nothing instead of a shell of thin slivers; sphere(style="octa") is now built as OpenSCAD builds it.

linear_extrude() takes v= and rotate_extrude() takes start=, as in OpenSCAD, and both read positional arguments in OpenSCAD's order; text(), textmetrics() and fontmetrics() take em=. The editor's argument hints for builtin modules now match OpenSCAD.
A new profile_time() times a block's script and geometry, or an expression, and prints the result; a new Profiling example shows how. Linux gets a proper desktop entry and .scad file association.
A trackpad swipe pans again and a Magic Mouse swipe zooms, told apart automatically; the Swipe scrolling setting from 1.65.3 is gone.
Files with non-breaking spaces in their code render again, and the mouse wheel zooms again on macOS and on Linux with high-resolution wheels.
Open and Save start in the folder you last used. The AI preferences page scrolls.
BOSL2's newer extrusion modules work again, Automatic Reload and Render no longer loops, and AI setup is explained step by step.
